reference: Borndorfer, Ralf, Martin Grotschel, and Marc E. Pfetsch. Models for line planning in public transport. Springer Berlin Heidelberg, 2008.
natural_language_example: A transit agency is deciding which candidate shuttle lines to activate and how frequently to operate each line. Every origin-destination demand pair can be served only by specified candidate lines. The agency minimizes fixed line activation cost, operating cost by frequency, and penalties for any unmet demand, subject to frequency bounds, a total vehicle-hours budget, and fixed transfer-node coverage requirements.
